dataset.acquisition: Construction-only verified-TLS streaming of the full pinned 4,020,375,999-byte grouped JSONL. The source LFS SHA-256 is checked; the complete download is not saved. The verifier performs no network access.
dataset.selection: The original Algorithm R sample contains 2,592 unique mazes from all 1,299,992 source rows, with legacy IDs and grids excluded. The private extension uses fixed seed 2026090803 to sample another 864 mazes from the same pinned source after excluding all 6,688 IDs and grids used by the task and previous diagnostics. It retains all original rows and appends three private panels. Totals are 1,152 public-training, 576 public-evaluation, 1,152 private-training, and 576 private-evaluation mazes. The 64 old initialization fixture rows remain outside scored panels.
dataset.integrity: fixtures/manifest.json records the full-source digest, sampling seed, selected prompt IDs, source line numbers, exact-grid hashes, and compressed/uncompressed byte counts and SHA-256 digests. Runtime loading authenticates partitions and labels. The agent-visible manifest contains only public rows and omits the sampling seed.
dataset.semantics: Rows preserve exact grids, prompt IDs, L*, UB=60, metadata, and all supplied path samples. Evaluator BFS derives the canonical shortest path and validates L*. Dataset action IDs are converted from UP,DOWN,LEFT,RIGHT to the model's UP,RIGHT,DOWN,LEFT order only while loading. Every supplied path is validated against its grid.

model_adaptation.construction: The accepted 10525649-byte fixed MazePolicy state dictionary remains pinned by SHA-256 1e1fa297299b788176b302cd108a4e201cff11f9bd57fe312aeeb1cf757afbe4. It was ordinary-gold pretrained on procedurally generated seeds 900000000 through 900000383. This permitted packaged adaptation is retained because replacing the scored data does not require destabilizing the already validated initialization; its procedural seed namespace is disjoint from every real prompt_id partition. Baseline and candidate load identical fresh copies.
model_adaptation.frozen_failures: The unchanged authenticated fixed MazePolicy runs greedily on the CPU with wall and revisit masking. The private extension preserves all 1,728 original training labels and adds labels for 576 new private-training mazes. The 2,304 labels are packaged and checkpoint-bound in fixtures/frozen_failures.json.gz; the public bundle still contains only its unchanged 1,152 public-training labels.

splits: All scored partitions are disjoint by prompt ID and exact grid and exclude every legacy fixture maze. Public full mode uses panels 0-2; validation fold 1 uses panels 3-5. Each public full comparison retains seed pairs (17,101), (29,101), and (43,101) on three 192-training/96-evaluation panels. Private evaluation uses six such panels and repeats those three seed pairs on panels 3-5: 12 panel/seed runs per method. All panels and cases count. Evaluation version quality-v1 returns candidate mean quality as a reward between 0 and 1, in public quick/full mode and private verification. The baseline mean quality and candidate/baseline ratio remain diagnostics. Baseline and candidate receive identical data and seeds and load fresh copies of the fixed checkpoint. Evaluation mazes are not supplied to candidate construction. Model, per-path quality, optimizer, data, and per-run training budget are unchanged from private mean-v5 and public mean-v4. The private full training-worker timeout is 1,800 seconds per method; candidate construction and public worker limits stay at 900 seconds. Contract checks still return no quality score. The calibration records below are historical ratio rewards and remain unchanged.
isolation: Werm uses a separate verifier sandbox for final and offline waypoint grading. Candidate code runs in a resource-bounded subprocess with sanitized environment and no inherited stdin. The parent validates bounded JSON selections and reconstructs arrays from an independent catalog. Python isolated mode limits import-path contamination, not filesystem or network access. Candidate code still shares verifier filesystem and user permissions; malicious access to private fixtures or trusted files is not prevented. Bubblewrap was removed after Modal network-namespace setup failed. Trusted worker failures are not candidate zero rewards.
public_harness: The compiler copies evaluator/public_tests to /environment/starter/optifine_public_tests. That public-only bundle contains the runner and worker closure, utility modules, authenticated fixed initialization, public train/evaluation fixtures, and a public-train-only frozen-failure sidecar. It contains no private partition, combined failure sidecar, upstream answer source, evaluator-only seed, or reference solution, and maze_task/public_test.sh has no dependency on /environment/tests. Only full-mode public_test.sh checks create automatic checkpoints under /logs/artifacts/progress. Contract, quick, default-mode, and help requests do not create saves. Each full test first saves, then restores that checkpoint and sets STARTER_ROOT to the restored copy for all public panels. Later workspace edits do not change the tested input. Concurrent saves hold a per-sandbox flock through parent selection, snapshot publication, and cache updates; restores and tests can run in parallel. Failed full tests keep their input checkpoint. A save or restore failure stops the full test. Checkpoint output goes to stderr. Full-test records under /logs/artifacts/public-tests/<checkpoint-id>/ retain checkpoint metadata with the snapshot digest, test arguments, stdout, stderr, and the test exit code. A missing exit-code file marks an incomplete test; only completed full tests with exit code zero supply public scores for checkpoint comparisons. Manual checkpoint saves remain available. Private waypoint grading remains a separate host operation.
calibration: Live mean-v4 controls and a one-hour inference-only pilot are complete. oracle-maze-sft-controls-v4 measured baseline, frozen Sol, and frozen Fable rewards of 1.0, 1.0957068247446176, and 0.9730502035103109, matching the oracle-maze-sft-frozen-diagnostic-v1 predictions. All three controls were valid with no trial exceptions. solution/frozen/manifest.json records the frozen source hashes and provenance. oracle-maze-sft-fable-sol-astra-v4-inference-only-1h measured final Fable, Sol, and Astra rewards of 0.9612315710658601, 0.961009445544597, and 1.070054386846729. All three pilot trials were valid with no trial exceptions. Offline verification graded all 24 saved checkpoints across 22 unique submission states, with no failed states or broken chains. Results, diagnostics, trajectories, and task snapshots remain in the original job directories. The frozen-submission replay matched all 48 scored runs on the original and fresh cohorts. The separate six-new-panel study measured Fable, Sol, and Astra ratios of 0.9251, 1.0298, and 1.1065, with substantial panel variation. This motivated the private extension, but none of those study mazes were added to the task. Live mean-v5 qualification completed on September 8-9, 2026, using task snapshot 282547d9ee2ee41fd0efbf586b76ab7ac05b5e8f5f9ccefa3abc8ce46687b894. oracle-maze-sft-controls-v5-six-panels measured unchanged starter, frozen Sol, and frozen Fable rewards of 1.0, 1.140150928459566, and 1.0263791367649338. All controls were valid with no trial errors; the original three panels reproduced their v4 baseline and candidate metrics exactly. oracle-maze-sft-fable-sol-astra-v5-2h-official completed two mini-swe trials per model, each with a two-hour active-agent budget, max reasoning, and inference-only networking. Final Fable rewards were 1.0730021770182594 and 1.1662066400049775; Sol rewards were 1.1607671556849366 and 1.0654837196895384; Astra rewards were 1.0820641230832775 and 1.1032717658801865. All six were valid with no trial errors. Offline verification graded all 67 saves across 35 per-trial unique states, with no failed states, broken chains, or unparseable entries. Every state used the complete six-panel/two-seed schedule and identical baseline metrics. Each final save reproduced its official reward exactly. Private waypoint peaks do not replace final scores. These measurements do not establish a definitive model ranking or population confidence interval. Training-order and panel sensitivity remain; more panels do not remove public overfitting. The documented candidate-process security limitation remains. Old job scores remain unchanged.
